production.note: US model years 2017-2020. Start: Ford's '2017 F-150 Raptor' key messages. End year is provisional: Auto123 (database) lists a 2020 F-150 Raptor SuperCab (auto123-raptor-2020); the 2021 Raptor is the next generation. No Ford page stating that 2020 was the last year of this generation was opened.

body.note: Ford: 'Available in both SuperCab and SuperCrew', including 'a Raptor-only SuperCab configuration with 134.2-inch wheelbase'. The standard car here is the SuperCab (5.5-ft box), the launch configuration; the SuperCrew is heavier.

displacementL.note: Ford: '3.5-liter'. The cc figure was not on a page opened for this car.

aspiration.note: Auto123 (database): 'Twin Turbo Regular Unleaded V-6' (2020 Raptor); Ford calls it the 'high-output EcoBoost V6'.

drivetrain.note: 'advanced four-wheel-drive torque-on-demand transfer case with Terrain Management System' (a two-speed 4x4 with an automatic 4A mode, like the Bronco Raptor).

powerHp.note: Quote: "All-new second-generation 3.5-liter high-output EcoBoost V6 engine producing out 510 lb.-ft. of torque and 450 horsepower". Same rating for 2019: The Auto Channel's spec list, 'HORSEPOWER/TORQUE: 450 hp @ 5,000 rpm/510- lb.-ft. @ 3,500 rpm' (autochannel-raptor-2019).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: a single named-author article, corroborated by an enthusiast site and a database. 2019 Raptor SuperCab. The Auto Channel (John Heilig) quote: "CURB WEIGHT: 5,552 lbs." F150Hub (f150hub-2nd-gen-raptor, enthusiast): "5,525 lbs(SuperCab)" for the 2017-on truck (0.5% lower). Auto123 (auto123-raptor-2020, database) for the 2020 SuperCab 5.5-ft box: "Curb Weight: 5508.00 (lbs)" (0.8% lower). Approximate figures ('5,600-pound', The Truth About Cars; '5600-5800 lb', Traction Life) are not used.

sources.title: 2019 Ford F-150 Raptor SuperCab Review by John Heilig
Car Specs Ford F-150 2020 Raptor 4WD SuperCab 5.5' Box

provisionalNote: Weight rests on one named-author article (The Auto Channel, 5,552 lb, 2019 SuperCab), corroborated within 1% by an enthusiast site (F150Hub, 5,525 lb) and a database (Auto123, 5,508 lb for 2020); a Ford specification sheet or a major magazine's specification panel would replace it. The last model year (2020) rests on Auto123 listing a 2020 Raptor; a Ford release on the 2021 Raptor would replace it. Reference year is 2019 because that is the year the article states; the 450 hp rating applied 2017-2020.
